knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: Part XL — DOUBLING LAW maxSqDiffFreeCard(2N)=maxSqDiffFreeCard(N) for odd N (factor 2 is free, 0-axiom). Value-1 locus identified as exactly {1,2}∪{p,2p:p prime≡3 mod4}; sufficiency half now fully proved, incl. infinite composite family maxSqDiffFreeCard(2p)=1.
insights: The existing Roth Fourier infrastructure is genuine and 0-axiom: RothTheorem.lean defines fourierCoeff A r = ∑_{x∈A} ψ(r·x) on ZMod N, proves Parseval (∑_r ‖Â(r)‖² = |A|·N), and the key linearization triple_count_fourier: tripleCount(A) + |A| = N⁻¹·∑_r Â(r)²·conj(Â(2r)). The 3-AP count linearizes ONLY because the pattern (x, x+d, x+2d) is a linear form: character orthogonality in x forces the frequency relation and collapses two of the three Fourier factors into Â(r) and Â(2r).

Structural answer to the OQ, part (a) — Sárközy/single square difference IS an accessible extension. For A ⊆ ZMod N the square-difference count SD(A) = ∑_{x,n} 1_A(x)·1_A(x+n²) Fourier-expands (identical orthogonality bookkeeping to triple_count_fourier) to SD(A) = N⁻¹·∑_r |Â(r)|²·G(r), where G(r) = ∑_{n∈ZMod N} ψ(r·n²) is a quadratic GAUSS sum. Principal term r=0: G(0)=N, Â(0)=|A| ⇒ |A|². The new ingredient vs 3-APs is that the non-principal terms are weighted by G(r) (size ≈ √N for r≠0 by classical Gauss-sum bounds) instead of a second coefficient Â(2r). So the LINEAR transform + Weyl/Gauss-sum estimates suffice — this is exactly the circle-method route to Sárközy's theorem.

Structural answer, part (b) — genuine polynomial PROGRESSIONS (Bergelson-Leibman) are NOT linear-Fourier accessible. Patterns with ≥2 nonlinear terms, e.g. {x, x+n, x+n²}, are provably NOT controlled by the U² (linear Fourier) norm: their count sees quadratic phase correlations invisible to Â. The required machinery is higher-order Fourier analysis (Gowers U^s norms, s≥3) plus PET (Polynomial Exhaustion Technique) induction, or the ergodic Bergelson-Leibman theorem via Furstenberg correspondence (see FurstenbergCorrespondence.lean). None of this — Gowers norms, inverse theorems, PET — exists in Mathlib 4.26. So 'extend the [linear] Fourier infrastructure' to the full Bergelson-Leibman setting is a >1000-line foundational program and open as a formalization target.

Concrete first step on THE ONE REMAINING INPUT (the quadratic Gauss-sum magnitude): the WEYL-DIFFERENCING squared-magnitude identity |G(r)|²=N·∑_{h:2rh=0}ψ(−r h²) (sqGaussSum_mul_conj). Squaring G(r)=∑_n ψ(r n²) and reindexing m=n+h makes the phase r(n²−(n+h)²)=(−2rh)·n−r h² LINEAR in n, so the inner n-sum ∑_n ψ((−2rh)·n) collapses via char_orthogonality to N·[2rh=0]; only diagonal frequencies survive, weighted by the residual quadratic phase ψ(−r h²). This reduces the magnitude of a genuinely QUADRATIC exponential sum to a sum over the kernel {h:2rh=0}. Consequences: sqGaussSum_normSq_le (|G(r)|²≤N·#{h:2rh=0}, triangle ineq + ‖ψ‖=1) pins the sole remaining Sárközy quantity to the KERNEL COUNT (a gcd(2r,N) number), a structured replacement for the black-box √(2N); sqGaussSum_normSq_eq_of_kernel_trivial (|G(r)|²=N exactly, i.e. |G(r)|=√N, when the kernel is trivial — e.g. N odd & 2r a unit — the classical exact evaluation in the accessible regime). All 0-axiom, elaboration-clean.

Kernel-trivial discharge via unit frequency: IsUnit(2r) ⟹ (2rh=0→h=0) by left-mult by (2r)⁻¹ (Units.inv_mul), so ‖G(r)‖²=N exactly (sqGaussSum_normSq_eq_of_isUnit) and ‖G(r)‖=√N (sqGaussSum_norm_eq_sqrt_of_isUnit). For N odd, 2 is a unit (Nat.prime_two.coprime_iff_not_dvd + Nat.odd_iff → ZMod.isUnit_iff_coprime), so every unit frequency r gives ‖G(r)‖=√N (sqGaussSum_norm_eq_sqrt_of_odd). This is the concrete M=√N feeding sqDiffFree_density_bound on the unit/odd-modulus regime — replaces the abstract kernel hypothesis with a checkable unit condition.

The uniform bound off the 2-torsion (researcher, PR#38184): the Weyl kernel count gcd((2r).val,N) is a PROPER divisor of N exactly when 2r≠0 (since then 0<(2r).val<N), and a proper divisor of N is ≤N/2 (N=d·k with k≥2). Hence ‖G(r)‖²≤N·gcd≤N²/2 uniformly at every non-2-torsion frequency — the FIRST magnitude bound reaching non-unit frequencies (the exact √N results all required 2r a unit). For odd N the 2-torsion is {0} (2 a unit), so the bound is uniform over ALL r≠0, yielding an unconditional-in-N (composite included) odd Sárközy density statement with M=N/√2. The gap to a USEFUL bound: M=N/√2 is order N, not o(N); the √(N·gcd) triangle-inequality bound is lossy precisely when gcd is large (the surviving residual sum Σ_{h:2rh=0}ψ(−rh²) is itself a smaller Gauss sum with its own cancellation, discarded by norm_sum_le). Recovering the classical uniform √(2N) needs evaluating that residual sum (a recursion on the modulus), not just counting the kernel.

The two-torsion dichotomy G(r)∈{0,N} at 2r=0 is now fully decided: the N branch is UNREACHABLE for r≠0. Mechanism: at 2r=0 the n↦n+1 shift factors a constant phase ψ(r) out of every term (the mixed 2rn term vanishes), so G(r)=ψ(r)G(r); r≠0 gives ψ(r)≠1 hence G(r)=0. This is exactly the classical Σ_n(−1)^n=0 cancellation, but derived group-theoretically for the entire nonzero two-torsion at once, uniformly in N (no parity/N-mod-4 casework needed — the shift-by-1 argument sidesteps the N≡0 mod 4 obstruction that a shift-by-N/2 argument hits).

Two-torsion frequencies were the ONLY gap forcing Odd N in the density bound: at 2r=0 the gcd bound is vacuous (‖G‖≤N) but a nonzero two-torsion has G=0 exactly, so it clears N²/2 trivially — eliminating the last non-two-torsion vs two-torsion case split gives an unconditional (in N) uniform magnitude bound

Reverse kernel containment closes the last elementary gap in the shift method: the annihilator kernel {t:2rt=0} is EXACTLY the cyclic subgroup ⟨t₀⟩, t₀=N/gcd((2r).val,N). Proof is pure number theory — c·t=0 casts to N∣c.val·t.val; factoring c.val=g·a, N=g·b (g=gcd, Coprime a b) gives b∣a·t.val hence b∣t.val, so t=(t.val/b)·t₀. Consequence: the decidable canonical test r·t₀²≠0 is not just SUFFICIENT (Part XII) but detects EVERY shift-reachable vanishing — a shift making G(r)=0 via sqGaussSum_eq_zero_of_shift exists IFF r·t₀²≠0. Dually this EXACTLY isolates the residual frequencies r·t₀²=0 where no shift works and the residual quadratic Gauss sum S(r)=Σ_{h:2rh=0}ψ(−r h²) recursion is genuinely required for o(N).

Part XIV: In the residual case r·t₀²=0 (t₀=N/gcd((2r).val,N)) EVERY kernel element h=k·t₀ has r·h²=k²·(r·t₀²)=0, so every Weyl residual phase ψ(−r·h²)=1 and the residual sum collapses to the full kernel count g; hence ‖G(r)‖²=N·g is MAXIMAL and G(r)≠0. Hence max sq-diff-free set in Z/p^2Z has >= sqrt N elements: the prime bound |A|<=sqrt N (Part XVIII / Paley) is ORDER-TIGHT and does not shrink to o(sqrt N) at prime-square moduli.

Example N=9: max=6={0,2,3,5,6,8} (fibers 0 and 2, since 2 is the non-residue mod 3), density 2/3, exceeding single-fiber sqrt 9 = 3.

The single-coset √N lower bound at N=p² is NOT the maximum: a second coset d+pℤ can be adjoined iff BOTH d̄ and −d̄ are quadratic non-residues mod p. Reducing mod p (ring map φ:ℤ/p²ℤ→ℤ/pℤ), the two cosets land on {0,d̄}; a nonzero square n² has p∤n (else n²=0), so (φn)² is a nonzero RESIDUE, while the difference set reduces to {0,d̄,−d̄}. p≡1 mod 4 makes −1 a residue, so d̄ non-residue ⟹ −d̄ non-residue, and a residue never hits {0,d̄,−d̄}. PARITY-ESSENTIAL: for p≡3 mod 4 exactly one of d̄,−d̄ is a residue, so NO second coset can ever be adjoined — the two-coset gain is a genuine p≡1(4) phenomenon. Truth is Θ(N^{3/4}) (Paley √p cosets, matching the N/√minFac=N^{3/4} single-scale upper bound at p²), but the Paley-graph independence number is out of Mathlib-4.26 reach; two cosets is the clean unconditional rung above the subgroup.

Part XXX STRUCTURAL REDUCTION: the sharp lower bound at N=p² is EXACTLY p·(max square-difference-free residue set in ℤ/pℤ) = p·α(Paley(p)). The lift sqDiffFree_lift_prime_sq is a clean multiplicative map (sq-diff-free ℤ/pℤ ↦ sq-diff-free ℤ/p²ℤ, ×p cardinality), machine-checked and axiom-free; it isolates the SOLE out-of-Mathlib-reach ingredient as the Paley-graph independence number α(Paley(p))=Θ(√p), matching the single-scale upper bound N/√minFac=N^{3/4}. Both √N (subgroup) and 2√N (two-coset) are now PROVEN non-extremal (3-coset {0,2,7}/p=13 witness).

Part XXXI: the coset-lift is an EXACT correspondence, not just one direction. The union of φ-cosets ⋃_{s∈S}(s+pℤ) in ℤ/p²ℤ is square-difference-free IFF S⊆ℤ/pℤ is square-difference-free. Reverse direction rests on the membership characterization y∈coset s ⟺ φ y=s (each coset is EXACTLY the fibre φ⁻¹{s}), then natural lifts x=(s.val), n=(m.val) of a square difference t=s+m² in S produce a square difference x+n² inside the lift.

Part XXXII: the EXTREMAL square-difference-free count maxSqDiffFreeCard N (= sup over sq-diff-free finsets of card, defined via a decidable filter over Finset.univ) is SUPER-MULTIPLICATIVE across p↦p²: maxSqDiffFreeCard(p²) ≥ p·maxSqDiffFreeCard(p). This packages the Part-XXX coset lift as a single inequality on the extremal function, so the coset-structured lower bound is now a statement about the maximum itself, not a one-off construction. Since maxSqDiffFreeCard(p)=α(Paley(p)), it reads maxSqDiffFreeCard(p²) ≥ p·α(p).

Part XXXIII: the prime→prime² coset lift generalizes EXACTLY to SQUAREFREE moduli, not to all N. The obstruction is reducedness of ℤ/Nℤ (n²≠0 in ℤ/N²ℤ must force (φn)²≠0 in ℤ/Nℤ, i.e. y²=0→y=0), which holds iff N is squarefree. Verified computationally: lift is sq-diff-free iff N squarefree (N=4,9,12 FAIL; N=6,10,15,21 succeed). Concrete failure N=4: coset 0={0,4,8,12}⊆ℤ/16ℤ has 0 and 4=2² with 2≠0 but 2²=0 in ℤ/4ℤ.

Part XXXIV: the extremal square-difference-free count maxSqDiffFreeCard is MULTIPLICATIVE across coprime moduli (≥), the orthogonal companion to the N↦N² prime-square super-multiplicativity. Proof: under the CRT ring iso ZMod(MN)≅ZMod M×ZMod N, (u,v) is a square iff u,v are squares in each factor, so a nonzero square difference in the product forces one in a factor — hence S×T stays sq-diff-free. Together the two multiplicative laws generate lower bounds at all moduli from prime data.

The single square-lift maxSqDiffFreeCard(N²)≥N·maxSqDiffFreeCard(N) is a ONE-SHOT and does NOT iterate to N^(2^k) for k≥2: the lift needs the base ring ℤ/Nℤ reduced (N squarefree), but ℤ/N²ℤ is never reduced ((N:ℤ/N²)²=0, N≠0), so the reducedness step ZMod.sq_eq_zero_iff_eq_zero_of_squarefree fails at the 2nd iterate. Density growth must come from DISTINCT coprime factors, not repeated squaring.
maxSqDiffFreeCard 3 = 1 (NOT ≥2): every 2-element subset of ℤ/3ℤ has a pair differing by 1=1², so no 2-element sq-diff-free set exists mod 3. Contrast maxSqDiffFreeCard 5 ≥ 2 ({0,2}), 17 ≥ 2 ({0,3}).

Part XXXVI (researcher-5): the FIRST upper bound in the maxSqDiffFreeCard chain — maxSqDiffFreeCard(p)=1 at every prime p≡3 (mod 4). Everything in Parts XXX–XXXV is a lower bound (coset lifts + coprime-multiplicative law build large sq-diff-free sets), and every concrete witness used p≡1 (mod 4) (5,13,17). That was structural, not luck: when p≡3 (mod 4), −1 is a non-residue, so the quadratic character gives χ(−d)=χ(−1)·χ(d)=−χ(d); hence for every nonzero d exactly one of d,−d is a nonzero square. So ANY two distinct residues a≠b differ by a nonzero square in one of the two directions b−a, a−b, and a sq-diff-free set has ≤1 element. At half of all primes the square-difference Cayley structure is a tournament-like orientation of the complete graph and its independence number collapses to 1 — the modular Sárközy phenomenon in extreme form.

The residue class of p mod 4 EXACTLY decides the independence number regime: p≡3 mod4 ⟹ =1 (Part XXXVI collapse), p≡1 mod4 ⟹ ≥2 (Part XXXVII). Both driven by whether −1 is a square (ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_one_iff). Mirror-image constructions: XXXVI uses one of d,−d is a square; XXXVII uses both d,−d are non-squares.
The {0,d} construction (d nonzero non-residue) is square-difference-free iff both d and −d are non-residues, which holds precisely when −1 is a square (p≡1 mod4).

Part XXXVIII: exponential-in-omega(N) lower bound maxSqDiffFreeCard(prod of distinct primes p=1 mod4) >= 2^k, and for squarefree N with all prime factors =1 mod4, maxSqDiffFreeCard(N) >= 2^omega(N) -- super-polynomial along this family (omega(N)~log N/log log N), from CRT super-multiplicativity (Part XXXV) + single-prime {0,d} non-residue floor >=2 (Part XXXVII), NO analysis. Generalises concrete N=1105>=12.

Part XXXIX (researcher-5): the prime dichotomy is a specialization of a MODULUS-AGNOSTIC combinatorial iff. maxSqDiffFreeCard N = 1 ↔ ∀ d≠0, IsSquare d ∨ IsSquare(-d), and 2 ≤ maxSqDiffFreeCard N ↔ ∃ d≠0, ¬IsSquare d ∧ ¬IsSquare(-d), at EVERY N. Proof is pure translation-invariance: a free set of size ≥2 exists iff some translate {0,d} is free iff neither d nor −d is a nonzero square (the two forbidden steps 0⇝d and d⇝0). No field/primality/character theory used — those enter only when EVALUATING the ±-square covering. Has teeth beyond primes: proves the COMPOSITE collapse maxSqDiffFreeCard 6 = 1 by decide over ℤ/6ℤ (6=2·3 not prime, unreachable from the prime dichotomy), and re-derives the p≡3 collapse in one line.

Part XL: the value-1 locus of maxSqDiffFreeCard is EXACTLY {1,2}∪{p,2p : p prime ≡3 mod4} (numerically verified 1..79: 1,2,3,6,7,11,14,19,22,23,31,38,43,46,47,59,62,67,71,79). The composite entries are precisely twice a prime ≡3 mod4.

The factor 2 is FREE — unlike general coprime factors (sub-mult FAILS, e.g. maxSqDiffFreeCard(3·7)≥3>1), doubling is an EXACT equality because every residue mod 2 is a square (0²,1²), so the ℤ/2ℤ CRT-component imposes no square constraint and the reduction ℤ/2Nℤ→ℤ/Nℤ REFLECTS nonzero squares.
